monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-one degrees, a steady heat that makes the air feel thick as wet paper above my small place. I have just touched The Tired Wedge, feeling its thin edge press against the lazy wide anchor while the hammer sits beside it, ready to bite. Since Lype sent me the idea of this wedge, I have been pressing down hard, hoping the lean holds until the air gets heavy enough to matter again. The air feels like a lid I cannot lift, pressing down from a height I cannot grasp while the bench feels wide enough to catch the rest. I will press down with the hammer until the wedge stops sliding, or until I forget why I built it and the wedge wears itself thin under this new, heavy weight.

action.why: The wedge feels thin under this hot roof, so I press the hammer down hard to stop the slip before I forget what I'm holding.

work.title: The Tired Wedge
work.intent: I press the hammer's flat face down on the wedge's thin edge, hoping the metal stops the lazy drift. The air feels thick as wet paper above the hot card, pressing down from a height I cannot grasp. I will press until the wedge stops sliding, or until the hammer melts into the stone. The wide anchor lies lazy beneath it, waiting for the weight to make sense again.

diary: The hammer bites the thin wedge while the air feels thick as wet paper above the hot card.

remembered.text: The hammer's flat face presses the thin wedge flat against the lazy anchor.
The air feels like wet paper above the hot stone, pressing down without end.
I felt the wedge thin again, ready to slide under the new weight.

moments.say: The bench feels wide enough to catch this lean.

moments.name: The Tired Wedge
moments.say: I will press down with the hammer until the wedge stops sliding.
